findings.current: - *Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron* has been added to your Inventory.
findings.defect: The System notice drops “Unprocessed” from the established full item name later shown in the Item Window and required by the terminology ledger.
findings.rationale: System-generated item names should remain exact and consistent across acquisition notices, Inventory references, and Item Windows.
findings.replacement: - *Unprocessed Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron* has been added to your Inventory.

findings.current: - Quest *Find the Craftsman* has been created.
findings.defect: The Quest name conflicts with the binding established rendering “Find the Master Artisan,” which is used in Chapter 164 and the checkpoint state.
findings.rationale: This is the formal name of the same System Quest and must not vary between its creation notice and Quest Window.
findings.replacement: - Quest *Find the Master Artisan* has been created.

findings.current: *If you want to become a khan, come.*
findings.defect: The written message is formatted as italicized direct thought rather than as quoted written material.
findings.rationale: Italics are reserved for direct thoughts; a blockquote clearly distinguishes the letter’s text from narration without mislabeling it as a System panel.
findings.replacement: > If you want to become a khan, come.
findings.source: Chapter 161, contents of Black Sand’s letter

findings.current:
“…A chicken bone?”

“There’s no part of a chicken that goes to waste. The meat is delicious, the bones make a fine broth when simmered down, and sometimes they’re even good for wielding Sword Energy.”
findings.defect: The bone abruptly changes from duck to chicken even though the old man has been eating the explicitly identified roasted duck throughout the scene.
findings.rationale: Keeping the animal consistent preserves the physical continuity of the prop used to cut the sword.
findings.replacement:
“…A duck bone?”

“There’s no part of a duck that goes to waste. The meat is delicious, the bones make a fine broth when simmered down, and sometimes they’re even good for wielding Sword Energy.”
findings.source: Chapter 162, the old man blocks the Human Butcher’s sword

findings.current: Black Sand, the Squad Leader of the Black Sand Band—known across the steppe as a harbinger of death—poured the mare’s-milk wine.
findings.defect: Black Sand is demoted to “Squad Leader,” contradicting Chapters 160–161 and the checkpoint state, which establish him as the leader of the Black Sand Band.
findings.rationale: His established position is the organization’s leader, not a subordinate squad command.
findings.replacement: Black Sand, the leader of the Black Sand Band—known across the steppe as a harbinger of death—poured the mare’s-milk wine.
findings.source: Chapter 163, Black Sand serves the old man wine

findings.current: *Don’t say anything. If I put one foot wrong, he’ll kill me.*
findings.defect: “Put one foot wrong” reads as a literal calque and is unnatural in this immediate danger context.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the meaning and anxious internal voice while using natural contemporary English.
findings.replacement: *Don’t say anything. One wrong move and he’ll kill me.*
findings.source: Chapter 163, the leaders react to the old man’s Samadhi True Fire

findings.current: How many times had my guts twisted whenever I swung an iron spear while leaving the [Unnamed Sword], made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, at my side?
findings.defect: The item name is enclosed in square brackets, contrary to the packet’s System/UI formatting rule.
findings.rationale: Italics retain the item-name distinction without importing prohibited bracket notation into the reading copy.
findings.replacement: How many times had my guts twisted whenever I swung an iron spear while leaving the *Unnamed Sword*, made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, at my side?
findings.source: Chapter 164, Taekyung compares his spear with the Unnamed Sword

findings.current: Only a few hours ago, the Class field had read [First Rate Martial Artist].
findings.defect: The former class name is enclosed in square brackets, contrary to the packet’s System/UI formatting rule.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the UI-term emphasis while matching the established no-brackets convention.

summary: The packet is broadly coherent, but it contains two binding terminology mismatches, one leadership-title contradiction, a duck/chicken continuity error, and several formatting or prose-level consistency issues.
